precepts.text: Remember Lot's wife: you are in this truth now, stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to please everybody and dropping by on birthdays, stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed as she was.
precepts.point: He overthrew the cities and all the plain, and Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt; why look back at a city like that unless you were not vexed with it and missed something in it?
precepts.why:
The angels pulled Lot into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness, and even blinded they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Then the angels took Lot out and gave them one order as the cities burned: don't look back. “And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.” “But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.”

Why would she look back? The city was being destroyed; she had just seen what happened in front of her house. She should have been glad to escape. Somebody was not vexed with the filthy conversation of that city; there was something in it she missed. That is why Luke also says, if you put your hand on the plow and look back, you are not worthy.

Christ said it in three words: “Remember Lot’s wife.” That is a warning for all of us: don't look back. You are in this truth now. Stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to be friends with everybody and please people, stop dropping by the house on their birthday. Focus on this truth and stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed just as Lot's wife was destroyed.

Judgment is coming to Esau, as Sodom's came. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to come out of her mentally, come back to the law, statutes and commandments, stop playing around in the truth, and keep the faith of Christ, without looking back.

precepts.text: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him. And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him. That brother is the children of thy people, per Leviticus 19:17.
precepts.point: Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ's seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance, the perpetual hatred Esau carries against his brother Jacob. Now the flip side: Peter asked, “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” Christ answered, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Christ offers boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to do the same.

Luke gives the terms: “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.” That brother is the children of thy people, as Leviticus 19:17 says. It is rebuke first, then repentance, then forgiveness.

“And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.” Why? Seven represents completion. The same way Christ forgave us when we were without sacrifice and without mercy: all our adulteries, fornication, lying and stealing during Assyria, Babylon, Persia and America, scattered in Africa in the dark ages doing all sorts of wicked things. Christ forgave all of that. That is why he said seventy times seven.

precepts.text: The earth was without form, and void; and God said, Let there be light.
precepts.point: In the beginning the earth existed first in God's mind. Made in his image, Israel can organize the kingdom in its mind before it is built.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
The kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. That is why the apostles asked in Acts whether Christ would at that time restore the kingdom to Israel, and why the Pharisees asked when it would come. “The kingdom of God cometh not with observation”. We look for it to come from somewhere outside. We externalize everything instead of taking up what is already in us. The Lord put a mind and a spirit in us to build and to organize.

You were made after the image of your Father, and Genesis shows how he created. “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form and void”. The earth did not yet exist physically, but it existed in God's mind. If he calls it earth, it existed; it existed in his mind. It was void in physical existence. “and darkness was upon the face of the deep”: the deep is the elements God used to fashion the earth. He manipulated the elements to materialize what was pictured in his mind. “And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters”: the Spirit moved upon the elements.

“And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” God imagined what light should be. “And God saw the light, that it was good”: when he created it, he compared it to the image in his mind, and it was good, meaning it conformed to his thoughts. He did the same with the earth: when it was all done he said it is good, because it matched the earth he had in mind before it was even created.

Because we are made in his image, we have the ability to do the same thing: to organize and put things together in our minds before they become physical. That is what Christ is saying: “Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” Everything you lay your eyes on, apart from the ground, the vegetation and the water, came from a thought. People cannot believe that IUIC can envision its buildings before bringing them into existence, but we are supposed to think like our Father. If filthy thoughts can become filthy words, actions, character and destiny, the same mind can materialize righteousness and build the city on the hill that is already in your mind.

“the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The Romans took the kingdom away from us by force. Part of the kingdom of heaven is being able to envision our nation and lay down the foundations for how it should operate, here on this earth, with our children, our women, everyone in order. Christ and the angels will come and give it to us physically, with power, but our minds have to be ready for it, so we need to be rehearsing it now.

precepts.text: As it was in the days of Lot, so shall it be in the day the Son of man is revealed; remember Lot's wife.
precepts.point: Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.
precepts.why:
“Remember Lot’s wife.” Three words, among the weightiest in the scriptures. Christ sets the days of Lot as the pattern for the day He is revealed: “they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded; But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all. Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.”

In that day, he on the housetop with his stuff in the house is not to come down to take it, and he in the field is not to return back. Then: “Remember Lot’s wife.” She looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt.

If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot’s wife.

precepts.text: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation; put on these attributes to bring forth the nation unto that kingdom.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
When the Pharisees demanded when the kingdom of God should come, Christ answered, “The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.”

The kingdom is within, and it is brought forth by putting on these attributes of Joseph: forgiveness, favor, righteousness, mercy, patience in the day of adversity. Applying them makes better men, women, brothers and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

precepts.text: The kingdom of God is within you; it is up to us to labour and bring forth the kingdom.
precepts.point: We cannot sit back knowing Christ is coming and not do the work; the time is short, and this is not our rest. We have to bring our brothers and sisters to repentance.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” The kingdom is not something to sit and wait for somewhere else; it is within us, so it is up to us to labour and bring it forth.

That is the answer to “How long are ye slack”. The land was given and they had to go possess it; the kingdom of God is within you and you have to do the work, bringing our brothers and sisters to repentance while the time is short.

precepts.text: Offences will come, it is inevitable; we build stronger bonds with brothers and sisters through adversity, so endeavor to keep the unity.
precepts.point: Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.
precepts.why:
“Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!” Offences will come; it is inevitable. Even in Israel there were slayers and avengers of blood, which is why the cities of refuge existed at all.

So when the offence comes, do not be the one through whom it comes. We build stronger bonds with brothers and sisters through adversity, so endeavor to keep the unity.

precepts.text: In that day, he on the housetop is not to come down to take his stuff, and he in the field is not to return back; remember Lot's wife, and be ready to lose everything and go.
precepts.point: Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back. Remember Lot’s wife.” When it is time to go, you do not go back for your stuff.

Remember Lot's wife: be ready to lose everything and go. Saul was entering into every house and haling men and women to prison, and that spirit is coming again, so you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime.

So remember, the angels said, let us tell Lot what is going to happen. And they let them in on the secret. The Most High did not broadcast that he was going to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah. He only told Abraham. And then just when the destruction was going to come, on the day of destruction, he sent the angels to get Lot out of the city because of Abraham. Because Lot was Abraham's nephew. So he had already told Abraham. Abraham was already looking, trying to save people. And the Lord already spoke to him and revealed to him destruction was coming.
